symptom: `mxcli test` on a headerless (mdl 0) `.test.mdl` printed one MDL-V1-SLASH and one MDL-DEPR001 warning per test, before any result — 104 warnings for a 52-test suite — although the `/` separators are what the test format requires. A suite with `mdl 1;` printed none, and `mxcli check` of the test file printed none either
cause: The warnings were about the script the runner generated, not the author's file. `GenerateTestFlows` and `GenerateTestRunner` kept the mdl 0 spellings — `CREATE OR REPLACE MICROFLOW` and a `/` line after every `END;` — on the theory that a headerless suite should get the script it always had; but mdl 0 warns on both, and the injecting `mxcli exec` printed those warnings verbatim. #943 had fixed the endpoint script and #847 the check rendering, both by writing the canonical form; the per-test generators were the last caller still switching on the version
file: `cmd/mxcli/testrunner/generator.go` (`createFlow` is now a constant `CREATE OR MODIFY MICROFLOW`; `writeFlowEnd` writes `END;` alone under every version)
insight: The canonical spelling is valid under mdl 0 as well, so the generators never needed a version switch for it — only the header follows the suite. Test generated scripts through `visitor.Build` and assert `LanguageNotes` and `Deprecations` are empty, with bodies valid under both versions so any note is the generator's; the previous test (`TestGeneratorsHeaderlessSuiteUnchanged`) only asserted the script parsed, which the warning-laden one did. Runtime control on an 11.12.2 app, same headerless file: main 2 MDL-V1-SLASH + 2 MDL-DEPR001, fix 0, both runs 2/2 PASS
